objective_text: Compare compute types, including containers, virtual machines, and functions
stem: Which compute option is event-driven and serverless, and charges only for the CPU time used while the code runs?
why_correct: Azure Functions is an event-driven, serverless compute option. An event wakes the function and Azure charges only for the CPU time used while it runs.
why_a_wrong: Virtual machines must be running for your app to work, so they are not billed only while code runs.
why_c_wrong: Azure Kubernetes Service orchestrates the lifecycle of containers and is not a serverless function service.
why_d_wrong: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps, not event-driven code.
author: claude

objective_text: Compare compute types, including containers, virtual machines, and functions
stem: How do containers differ from virtual machines when it comes to the operating system?
option_a: Each container needs its own operating system that you manage
option_b: Unlike a virtual machine, you do not manage the operating system for a container
option_c: Containers cannot run on a host that also runs other containers
option_d: Containers are slow to start and cannot be scaled dynamically
why_correct: Unlike virtual machines, you do not manage the operating system for a container. Containers are lightweight and designed to be created, scaled out and stopped dynamically.
why_a_wrong: Each VM runs its own OS that you manage, but you do not manage one for a container.
why_c_wrong: You can run multiple containers on a single physical or virtual host.
why_d_wrong: Containers are lightweight and can restart quickly after a crash or interruption.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual machine options, including Azure virtual machines, Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets, availability sets, and Azure Virtual Desktop
stem: A team needs a group of identical, load-balanced virtual machines that scale out and in automatically with demand. Which Azure feature fits?
why_correct: Virtual Machine Scale Sets let you create and manage groups of identical, load-balanced VMs that can scale out or in automatically based on demand or schedules.
why_b_wrong: An availability set improves resiliency within a region using fault and update domains, rather than scaling.
why_c_wrong: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps and is not a scaling group.
why_d_wrong: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and does not scale VMs.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual machine options, including Azure virtual machines, Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets, availability sets, and Azure Virtual Desktop
stem: In an availability set, what is a fault domain?
option_a: VMs that can be rebooted together during planned maintenance
option_b: VMs that share a potential power or network failure point
option_c: A copy of a VM kept in another region
why_correct: A fault domain is a group of VMs that share a potential power or network failure point. Spreading VMs across fault domains reduces the chance they all fail together.
why_a_wrong: That describes an update domain, not a fault domain.
why_c_wrong: Availability sets improve resiliency inside a region, not by copying VMs to another region.
why_d_wrong: Subscriptions are billing and management units, not part of an availability set.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual machine options, including Azure virtual machines, Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets, availability sets, and Azure Virtual Desktop
stem: A company wants staff and contractors to securely reach Windows desktops and apps hosted in Azure from many kinds of devices. Which service fits?
why_correct: Azure Virtual Desktop is a desktop and application virtualization service that lets users securely access Windows desktops and apps from many device types and locations.
why_b_wrong: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and does not deliver desktops.
why_c_wrong: ExpressRoute is a private network connection, not a desktop service.
why_d_wrong: Azure Functions runs event-driven code and does not deliver desktops.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe the resources required for virtual machines
stem: Which set of choices must you make when you provision an Azure virtual machine?
option_a: Compute size, storage disks and networking
why_correct: A VM needs compute (its size, such as cores and RAM), storage (disks) and networking (a virtual network, public IP address and port configuration).
why_b_wrong: Tags and budgets are for organizing and tracking cost, not what a VM is built from.
why_c_wrong: Blobs, queues and tables are Azure Storage services, not VM building blocks.
why_d_wrong: Management groups, policies and locks govern resources and are not what a VM is built from.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe application hosting options, including web apps, containers, and virtual machines
stem: A team wants to host a web app and a REST API without managing the underlying infrastructure, with automatic scaling. Which option fits best?
why_correct: App Service lets you build and host web apps, background jobs, mobile back ends and REST APIs without managing infrastructure, with automatic scaling and high availability.
why_a_wrong: VMs give maximum control but you manage the hosting environment yourself.
why_c_wrong: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps rather than hosting your web apps.
why_d_wrong: VPN Gateway is a network connection service, not an app hosting option.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe application hosting options, including web apps, containers, and virtual machines
stem: A team needs maximum control of its hosting environment and wants to configure it exactly as it likes. Which hosting option fits?
why_correct: Virtual machines give you maximum control of the hosting environment and let you configure it exactly how you want.
why_a_wrong: App Service lets you host apps without managing infrastructure, so you control less.
why_b_wrong: Azure Functions is event-driven serverless compute with no servers to manage.
why_d_wrong: Container Instances is a simple way to run containers without managing virtual machines.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, Azure virtual subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
stem: Which service lets Azure resources talk to each other, to the internet and to on-premises computers, using an isolated private IP range that is not internet routable?
why_correct: Azure virtual networks let you create isolated networks whose IP range exists only within the network and is not internet routable. You can divide it into subnets.
why_a_wrong: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains for name resolution.
why_c_wrong: ExpressRoute is a private connection from on-premises to Azure, not the isolated network itself.
why_d_wrong: Azure Functions runs event-driven code and is not a network.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, Azure virtual subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
stem: Two virtual networks in different regions need to exchange private traffic that travels on the Microsoft backbone and never enters the public internet. What should be used?
why_correct: Peering lets two virtual networks connect directly. Traffic between them is private, travels on the Microsoft backbone, and can cross regions.
why_a_wrong: A public endpoint has a public IP address and can be reached from anywhere.
why_b_wrong: An alias record in Azure DNS points a name at an Azure resource.
why_c_wrong: A subnet divides one virtual network's address space and does not connect two networks.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, Azure virtual subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
stem: A company wants an encrypted tunnel over the public internet between its on-premises datacenter and an Azure virtual network. Which service fits?
why_correct: Azure VPN Gateway sends encrypted traffic through a private tunnel across the public internet, and supports site-to-site connections to on-premises datacenters.
why_a_wrong: ExpressRoute is a private connection that does not go over the public internet.
why_b_wrong: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and does not create tunnels.
why_d_wrong: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, Azure virtual subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
stem: A company wants a private connection from its on-premises network to Azure, provided with a connectivity provider, that does not go over the public internet. Which service fits?
why_correct: ExpressRoute is a private connection from on-premises infrastructure to Azure through a connectivity provider. The connections do not go over the public internet.
why_a_wrong: VPN Gateway encrypts traffic but sends it across the public internet.
why_c_wrong: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and is not a network connection.
why_d_wrong: App Service hosts apps and is not a network connection.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe virtual networking, including the purpose of Azure virtual networks, Azure virtual subnets, peering, Azure DNS, Azure VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute
stem: A company wants to host the DNS records for its domain in Azure, managed with the same credentials and tools as its other Azure services. Which service fits?
why_correct: Azure DNS is a hosting service for DNS domains that provides name resolution using Azure infrastructure, managed with the same credentials, APIs, tools and billing as other Azure services.
why_a_wrong: VPN Gateway creates encrypted tunnels and does not host DNS records.
why_b_wrong: ExpressRoute is a private network connection and does not host DNS records.
why_c_wrong: Peering connects two virtual networks and does not host DNS records.
author: claude

stem: Which description fits a private endpoint?
option_a: It has a public IP address and can be reached from anywhere in the world
option_b: It exists within a virtual network and has a private IP address from that network's address space
option_c: It is an encrypted tunnel across the public internet
option_d: It is a set of DNS records for a domain
why_correct: Private endpoints exist within a virtual network and have a private IP address from that network's address space.
why_c_wrong: An encrypted tunnel over the internet is what VPN Gateway provides.
why_d_wrong: DNS records are hosted by Azure DNS and are not endpoints.
author: claude
